# Template: ppf
A production possibilities frontier (PPF) between two goods: a bowed-out (concave, increasing-opportunity-cost) or straight-line (constant- opportunity-cost) curve from the y-axis intercept to the x-axis intercept, the attainable region shaded underneath it, and optional labeled points that are efficient (on the frontier), inefficient (inside it, wasting resources), or unattainable (outside it, beyond current capacity). Choose this scene for ANY request about the production possibilities frontier, PPF, production possibilities curve, opportunity cost, scarcity, productive efficiency, or a classic "guns and butter" tradeoff. `indifference_curves` adds community indifference curves and the point where the highest attainable one is TANGENT to the frontier — the society-chooses-a-point-on-the-frontier figure, where the frontier alone only says which points are feasible. The tangency is computed, not eyeballed: the curve touches the frontier at `optimum_at` and lies inside the attainable set everywhere else.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "good_x": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label for the good on the x-axis (default \"Good X\")."
  },
  "good_y": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label for the good on the y-axis (default \"Good Y\")."
  },
  "bowed": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Concave, bowed-out frontier from increasing opportunity cost (default true); false draws a straight-line frontier (constant opportunity cost)."
  },
  "points": {
   "type": "array",
   "items": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
     "x_share": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "0-1: how far along the frontier, from the y-intercept (0) to the x-intercept (1), this point's direction from the origin is taken from."
     },
     "label": {
      "type": "string"
     },
     "kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
       "efficient",
       "inefficient",
       "unattainable"
      ],
      "description": "efficient (default) sits ON the frontier; inefficient sits inside it (feasible but wasteful); unattainable sits outside it (infeasible)."
     }
    },
    "required": [
     "x_share",
     "label"
    ]
   },
   "description": "Labeled reference points relative to the frontier."
  },
  "shade_attainable": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Shade the attainable region under the frontier (default true)."
  },
  "indifference_curves": {
   "type": "integer",
   "enum": [
    0,
    1,
    2,
    3
   ],
   "description": "Community indifference curves against the frontier (default 0, none): 1 draws only the utility-maximizing curve, tangent to the frontier; 2 adds a lower, attainable curve; 3 adds a higher, unattainable one too. Numeric, so it can be animated from 0."
  },
  "optimum_at": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "0-1: where along the frontier, from the y-intercept (0) to the x-intercept (1), the tangency sits (default 0.5, the middle). Clamped to 0.08-0.92 so the implied preferences stay sane. Animate it to slide society's chosen point along the frontier."
  },
  "optimum_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label on the tangency dot (default \"Optimum\")."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (one group with both axis lines and their captions)
- frontier: the production possibilities frontier curve
- attainable: the shaded attainable region under the frontier, present when shade_attainable
- pt_<i>: marker for points[i]
- pt_label_<i>: its label
- ic_1 / ic_2 / ic_3: the indifference curve(s) actually drawn, in order below/at/above the optimum (only as many as `indifference_curves` requests, so with 1 the single curve is ic_1 and it IS the tangent one)
- label_ic_1 / label_ic_2 / label_ic_3: each drawn curve's label
- optimum: dot where the highest attainable indifference curve touches the frontier, present when indifference_curves > 0
- optimum_label: the optimum's label
Examples:
Request: "Draw a production possibilities frontier for guns and butter." → params: {"good_x":"Guns","good_y":"Butter"}
Request: "Show a production possibilities frontier with an unattainable combination of healthcare and education." → params: {"good_x":"Healthcare","good_y":"Education","points":[{"x_share":0.5,"label":"Unattainable mix","kind":"unattainable"}]}
Request: "Add indifference curves to the PPF and show which point society actually chooses." → params: {"good_x":"Healthcare","good_y":"Everything else","indifference_curves":3,"optimum_at":0.45}

In YAML: `template: ppf` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
